<script lang="ts">
import { Comment, defineComponent, Fragment, h, Text, type VNode } from 'vue'

/** Unwraps v-for lists and drops comments, leaving one entry per avatar. */
function flatten(nodes: VNode[]): VNode[] {
  return nodes.flatMap((node) => {
    if (node.type === Comment || node.type === Text) return []
    if (node.type === Fragment) return flatten((node.children as VNode[]) ?? [])
    return [node]
  })
}

export default defineComponent({
  name: 'AvatarGroup',
  props: {
    /** Most avatars to show. The rest are counted in a "+3" at the end. */
    max: { type: Number, default: undefined },
    /** Accessible name of the group, e.g. "Team members". */
    label: { type: String, default: undefined },
  },
  setup(props, { slots }) {
    return () => {
      const avatars = flatten(slots.default?.() ?? [])
      const shown = props.max !== undefined && avatars.length > props.max ? avatars.slice(0, props.max) : avatars
      const hidden = avatars.length - shown.length
      return h('div', { class: 'er-avatar-group', role: 'group', 'aria-label': props.label }, [
        ...shown,
        hidden > 0 ? h('span', { class: 'er-avatar er-avatar-more', role: 'img', 'aria-label': `${hidden} more` }, `+${hidden}`) : null,
      ])
    }
  },
})
</script>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { nextTick, ref, useId } from 'vue'
import { Portal } from '../../lib/primitive'
import { provideDropdownMenu } from '../dropdown-menu/context'
import { provideContextMenu } from './context'

const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })

/** An invisible point placed where the pointer was. The menu positions itself against it like any trigger. */
const anchor = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null)
const point = ref({ x: 0, y: 0 })
const focusFirst = ref(false)

function setOpen(next: boolean) {
  open.value = next
}

// The same state the dropdown menu's parts expect, so its items, groups and submenus all work inside.
provideDropdownMenu({ open, setOpen, anchor, focusFirst, triggerId: useId(), contentId: useId() })

provideContextMenu({
  openAt: async (x, y, fromKeyboard) => {
    // A second right-click while open moves the menu: close first so it reopens at the new point.
    if (open.value) {
      open.value = false
      await nextTick()
    }
    point.value = { x, y }
    focusFirst.value = fromKeyboard
    await nextTick()
    open.value = true
  },
})
</script>

<template>
  <slot :open="open" />
  <Portal>
    <span ref="anchor" class="er-context-menu-point" aria-hidden="true" :style="{ left: `${point.x}px`, top: `${point.y}px` }" />
  </Portal>
</template>

<style>
@layer components {
  .er-context-menu-point {
    position: fixed;
    width: 0;
    height: 0;
    pointer-events: none;
  }
}
</style>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { DropdownMenuContent } from '../dropdown-menu'
</script>

<template>
  <!-- The dropdown menu's own panel, opening down and to the right of the pointer. -->
  <DropdownMenuContent side="bottom" align="start" :side-offset="2">
    <slot />
  </DropdownMenuContent>
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Component } from 'vue'
import { Primitive } from '../../lib/primitive'
import { useContextMenu } from './context'

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    as?: string | Component
    /** Use the single child as the right-click area instead of wrapping it in an element. */
    asChild?: boolean
    disabled?: boolean
  }>(),
  { as: 'div' },
)

const menu = useContextMenu()

function onContextMenu(event: MouseEvent) {
  if (props.disabled) return
  event.preventDefault()
  // The Menu key and Shift+F10 also fire this event, without a real pointer position.
  const fromKeyboard = event.button !== 2 && event.detail === 0
  if (fromKeyboard) {
    const box = (event.currentTarget as HTMLElement).getBoundingClientRect()
    menu.openAt(box.left + Math.min(box.width / 2, 24), box.top + Math.min(box.height / 2, 24), true)
  } else {
    menu.openAt(event.clientX, event.clientY, false)
  }
}
</script>

<template>
  <Primitive :as="as" :as-child="asChild" @contextmenu="onContextMenu">
    <slot />
  </Primitive>
</template>

  contentId: useId(),

import type { Component } from 'vue'
import { Primitive } from '../../lib/primitive'
import { useDropdownMenu } from './context'

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    /** Tag or component to render — use "a" (or a router link) for navigation items. */
    as?: string | Component
    disabled?: boolean
    variant?: 'default' | 'destructive'
  }>(),
  { as: 'div', variant: 'default' },
)

const emit = defineEmits<{
  /** Fired when the item is chosen. Call event.preventDefault() to keep the menu open. */
  select: [event: Event]
}>()

const menu = useDropdownMenu()

function onClick(event: MouseEvent) {
  if (props.disabled) {
    event.preventDefault()
    return
  }
  emit('select', event)
  if (!event.defaultPrevented) menu.setOpen(false)
}

function onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
  if (event.key !== 'Enter' && event.key !== ' ') return
  event.preventDefault()
  ;(event.currentTarget as HTMLElement).click()
}

function onPointerMove(event: PointerEvent) {
  if (!props.disabled) (event.currentTarget as HTMLElement).focus({ preventScroll: true })
}

function onPointerLeave(event: PointerEvent) {
  ;(event.currentTarget as HTMLElement).closest<HTMLElement>('[role="menu"]')?.focus({ preventScroll: true })
}
</script>

    role="menuitem"
    tabindex="-1"
    class="er-menu-item"
    :data-variant="variant"
    :data-disabled="disabled ? '' : undefined"

    @keydown="onKeydown"

    @pointerleave="onPointerLeave"

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref, useId, watch } from 'vue'
import { provideDropdownMenuSub, useDropdownMenu } from './context'

const menu = useDropdownMenu()
const open = ref(false)
const focusFirst = ref(false)
const anchor = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null)
const content = ref<HTMLElement | null>(null)

let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
function cancelClose() {
  clearTimeout(timer)
}

function setOpen(next: boolean, first = false) {
  cancelClose()
  focusFirst.value = next && first
  open.value = next
}

provideDropdownMenuSub({
  open,
  setOpen,
  focusFirst,
  anchor,
  content,
  contentId: useId(),
  // The short wait lets the pointer travel diagonally from the trigger into the submenu without it closing.

    cancelClose()
    timer = setTimeout(() => setOpen(false), 150)
  },
  cancelClose,
})

// so the menu can hand it back to the button that opened it.
watch(menu.open, (isOpen) => {
  if (isOpen || !open.value) return
  if (content.value?.contains(document.activeElement)) anchor.value?.focus({ preventScroll: true })
  setOpen(false)
})

onBeforeUnmount(cancelClose)
</script>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref } from 'vue'

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    /** What goes full screen: a CSS selector, an element, or a function returning one. Defaults to the whole page. */
    target?: string | HTMLElement | (() => HTMLElement | null | undefined)
    enterLabel?: string
    exitLabel?: string
  }>(),
  { enterLabel: 'Enter full screen', exitLabel: 'Exit full screen' },
)

const emit = defineEmits<{
  change: [active: boolean]
  /** The browser refused, or the target could not be found. */
  error: [error: unknown]
}>()

const supported = ref(false)
const active = ref(false)

// Safari on older systems still uses prefixed names.
type PrefixedDocument = Document & { webkitFullscreenElement?: Element | null; webkitExitFullscreen?: () => Promise<void>; webkitFullscreenEnabled?: boolean }
type PrefixedElement = HTMLElement & { webkitRequestFullscreen?: () => Promise<void> }

function element(): HTMLElement | null {
  const target = props.target
  if (!target) return document.documentElement
  if (typeof target === 'string') return document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(target)
  return (typeof target === 'function' ? target() : target) ?? null
}

const current = () => document.fullscreenElement ?? (document as PrefixedDocument).webkitFullscreenElement ?? null

function sync() {
  const next = current() !== null && current() === element()
  if (next !== active.value) emit('change', next)
  active.value = next
}

async function toggle() {
  try {
    if (current()) {
      await (document.exitFullscreen?.() ?? (document as PrefixedDocument).webkitExitFullscreen?.())
      return
    }
    const el = element() as PrefixedElement | null
    if (!el) throw new Error('The element to show full screen was not found.')
    await (el.requestFullscreen?.() ?? el.webkitRequestFullscreen?.())
  } catch (error) {
    emit('error', error)
  }
}

onMounted(() => {
  // iPhones do not allow page elements to go full screen at all; the button is left out there.
  supported.value = document.fullscreenEnabled ?? (document as PrefixedDocument).webkitFullscreenEnabled ?? false
  document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', sync)
  document.addEventListener('webkitfullscreenchange', sync)
})

onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  document.removeEventListener('fullscreenchange', sync)
  document.removeEventListener('webkitfullscreenchange', sync)
})
</script>

<template>
  <!-- The name says what a press will do, and changes with the state. Escape always leaves full screen too. -->
  <button v-if="supported" type="button" class="er-fullscreen-button" :aria-label="active ? exitLabel : enterLabel" :title="active ? exitLabel : enterLabel" :data-state="active ? 'on' : 'off'" @click="toggle">

</template>

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{

    openDelay?: number
    /** Time the card stays after the pointer leaves, in ms — long enough to move into it. */
    closeDelay?: number

function hide(immediate = false) {
  clearTimeout(timer)
  if (immediate) open.value = false
  else timer = setTimeout(() => (open.value = false), props.closeDelay)

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    /** The values, oldest first. */
    data: readonly number[]
    width?: number
    height?: number
  }>(),
  { width: 96, height: 32 },
)

// Room for the 2px line and the end dot, so neither is cut off at the edges.
const PAD = 4

const points = computed(() => {
  const values = props.data.filter((value) => Number.isFinite(value))
  if (values.length < 2) return []
  const min = Math.min(...values)
  const span = Math.max(...values) - min || 1
  const step = (props.width - PAD * 2) / (values.length - 1)
  return values.map((value, index) => ({
    x: PAD + index * step,
    y: props.height - PAD - ((value - min) / span) * (props.height - PAD * 2),
  }))
})
const line = computed(() => points.value.map((point, index) => `${index ? 'L' : 'M'}${point.x},${point.y}`).join(''))
const last = computed(() => points.value[points.value.length - 1])
</script>

<template>
  <!-- A shape, not a readout: the number beside it carries the value, so this is hidden from screen readers. -->
  <svg class="er-sparkline" :width="width" :height="height" aria-hidden="true">
    <path :d="line" />
    <circle v-if="last" :cx="last.x" :cy="last.y" r="3" />

<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'
import { Select, SelectContent, SelectItem, SelectTrigger } from '../select'

// Attributes such as id and aria-invalid go to the button, so <Label for="..."> works.
defineOptions({ inheritAttrs: false })

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    /** Minutes between the times on offer. */
    step?: number
    /** Earliest and latest times on offer, as 'HH:MM' in 24-hour time. */
    min?: string
    max?: string
    /** Submit the value with a form under this name, as 'HH:MM'. */
    name?: string
    disabled?: boolean
    placeholder?: string
    /** Language for how times are written. Fixed by default so server and browser render the same text. */
    locale?: string
    /** Write times with am / pm. Defaults to what the locale uses. */
    hour12?: boolean
  }>(),
  { step: 30, min: '00:00', max: '23:59', placeholder: 'Pick a time', locale: 'en-US', hour12: undefined },
)

/** The time as 'HH:MM' in 24-hour time, the same as <input type="time">. */
const value = defineModel<string>()

const toMinutes = (time: string) => {
  const match = /^(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})$/.exec(time)
  return match ? Number(match[1]) * 60 + Number(match[2]) : Number.NaN
}
const toTime = (minutes: number) => `${String(Math.floor(minutes / 60)).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(minutes % 60).padStart(2, '0')}`

const format = computed(() => new Intl.DateTimeFormat(props.locale, { hour: 'numeric', minute: '2-digit', hour12: props.hour12, timeZone: 'UTC' }))
const label = (time: string) => format.value.format(new Date(toMinutes(time) * 60_000))

const times = computed(() => {
  const start = Math.max(0, toMinutes(props.min) || 0)
  const end = Math.min(24 * 60 - 1, Number.isNaN(toMinutes(props.max)) ? 24 * 60 - 1 : toMinutes(props.max))
  const list: string[] = []
  for (let minutes = start; minutes <= end; minutes += Math.max(1, props.step)) list.push(toTime(minutes))
  // A value that is not on a step (set from saved data, say) still appears, in its place.
  if (value.value && !Number.isNaN(toMinutes(value.value)) && !list.includes(value.value)) list.push(value.value)
  return list.sort((a, b) => toMinutes(a) - toMinutes(b))
})
</script>

<template>
  <Select v-model="value" :name="name" :disabled="disabled">
    <SelectTrigger v-bind="$attrs" :placeholder="placeholder" class="er-time-picker" />
    <SelectContent>
      <SelectItem v-for="time in times" :key="time" :value="time">{{ label(time) }}</SelectItem>
    </SelectContent>
  </Select>
</template>

<style>
@layer components {

    font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  }
}
</style>

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, ref, useId } from 'vue'
import { provideTooltip } from './context'

const props = withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    /** Hover time before the tooltip appears, in ms. Keyboard focus shows it immediately. */
    delay?: number
    disabled?: boolean
  }>(),
  { delay: 300 },
)

const open = defineModel<boolean>('open', { default: false })
let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined

function show(immediate = false) {
  clearTimeout(timer)
  if (props.disabled) return
  if (immediate || open.value) open.value = true
  else timer = setTimeout(() => (open.value = true), props.delay)
}

function hide(immediate = false) {
  clearTimeout(timer)
  if (immediate) open.value = false
  // The grace period lets the pointer travel from the trigger onto the tooltip.
  else timer = setTimeout(() => (open.value = false), 100)
}

onBeforeUnmount(() => clearTimeout(timer))

provideTooltip({ open, show, hide, anchor: ref(null), contentId: useId() })
</script>

<template>
  <slot :open="open" />
</template>

<script setup lang="ts">
import type { Component } from 'vue'
import { Primitive, toElement } from '../../lib/primitive'
import { useTooltip } from './context'

withDefaults(
  defineProps<{
    as?: string | Component
    /** Use the single child (e.g. a Button) as the trigger instead of rendering one. */
    asChild?: boolean
  }>(),
  { as: 'button' },
)

const tooltip = useTooltip()

function setAnchor(target: unknown) {
  tooltip.anchor.value = toElement(target)
}

function onPointerEnter(event: PointerEvent) {
  if (event.pointerType !== 'touch') tooltip.show()
}

function onFocus(event: FocusEvent) {
  // Only for keyboard focus — a click also focuses, and should not pop a tooltip.
  if ((event.target as HTMLElement).matches(':focus-visible')) tooltip.show(true)
}

function onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent) {
  if (event.key === 'Escape') tooltip.hide(true)
}
</script>

<template>
  <Primitive
    :ref="setAnchor"
    :as="as"
    :as-child="asChild"
    :type="as === 'button' && !asChild ? 'button' : undefined"
    :aria-describedby="tooltip.open.value ? tooltip.contentId : undefined"
    :data-state="tooltip.open.value ? 'open' : 'closed'"
    @pointerenter="onPointerEnter"
    @pointerleave="tooltip.hide()"
    @pointerdown="tooltip.hide(true)"
    @focus="onFocus"
    @blur="tooltip.hide(true)"
    @keydown="onKeydown"
  >
    <slot />
  </Primitive>
</template>

  display: { step: 6, tag: 'h1' },
  h1: { step: 5, tag: 'h1' },
  h2: { step: 4, tag: 'h2' },
  h3: { step: 3, tag: 'h3' },

<script setup lang="ts">
import { onBeforeUnmount, onMounted, ref } from 'vue'

const emit = defineEmits<{
  /** The browser refused: usually low battery or a power-saving mode. */
  error: [error: unknown]
}>()

/** Whether the screen should be kept awake. */
const active = defineModel<boolean>({ default: false })

const supported = ref(false)
let lock: { release: () => Promise<void>; addEventListener: (type: 'release', listener: () => void) => void } | undefined

type WakeLockNavigator = Navigator & { wakeLock?: { request: (type: 'screen') => Promise<NonNullable<typeof lock>> } }

async function acquire() {
  try {
    lock = await (navigator as WakeLockNavigator).wakeLock!.request('screen')
    // The system can take the lock away at any time (the tab is hidden, the battery runs low).
    lock.addEventListener('release', () => {
      lock = undefined
    })
  } catch (error) {
    active.value = false
    emit('error', error)
  }
}

async function toggle() {
  // Worked out first and used directly: when bound with v-model, `active` only changes once the parent has re-rendered.
  const next = !active.value
  active.value = next
  if (next) await acquire()
  else await lock?.release()
}

// Browsers drop the lock whenever the tab is hidden; take it again when the reader comes back.
function onVisibility() {
  if (active.value && !lock && document.visibilityState === 'visible') void acquire()
}

onMounted(() => {
  supported.value = 'wakeLock' in navigator
  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility)
  if (supported.value && active.value) void acquire()
})

onBeforeUnmount(() => {
  document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', onVisibility)
  void lock?.release()
})
</script>

<template>
  <!-- Rendered only where it can work: a switch that does nothing is worse than no switch. -->
  <button v-if="supported" type="button" class="er-wake-lock" :aria-pressed="active" :data-state="active ? 'on' : 'off'" @click="toggle">
